summary.text: Ramon Mora Jr. is a healthcare worker from Vineland running as an independent for New Jersey's 2nd District. He says he grew up in Section 8 housing and experienced periods of homelessness, and that a back injury kept him from working for years. His campaign emphasizes affordability, government-accountability reforms and replacing ICE.

paragraphs.text: Mora says he was born and raised in South Jersey and has lived there for 31 years; Front Runner New Jersey describes him as from Vineland.
He graduated from Vineland High School and earned an associate degree from Atlantic Cape Community College in 2018, which Front Runner New Jersey reports was in nursing.
He has worked in healthcare, including, according to WHYY, as a nurse technician.
Mora describes growing up in a Section 8 housing neighborhood and experiencing periods of homelessness, including as a teenager and again around age 20.

Mora says a serious back injury paused his life for years and that he focused on physical recovery for about five years before this campaign; WHYY reports he said he had been on track to become a registered nurse until the injury, which resulted from a motorcycle crash.
He says he is running as a Progressive Independent after a falling out with the Democratic Party, that he is not a career politician, and, per WHYY, that he has no formal political experience.
